points.description: States the correct order: B least probable, then C, then A most probable (B < C < A, i.e. BCA).
points.partial_credit: Half if order is mostly right but with a minor slip (e.g. reversed notation), otherwise none.

points.description: Gives a valid justification: B is a subset/special case/more specific than C, and C is a subset/special case of A; OR correct probability calculations/formulas showing P(B)<P(C)<A (e.g. P(B)=0.6^3*0.4^3≈0.014, P(C)=20*P(B)≈0.28, P(A)≈0.82; rounding to 2 d.p. allowed).
points.partial_credit: Half if justification covers only one of the two relations (B vs C or C vs A) or has a minor calculation slip; none if justification is missing or vague.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the correct order BCA plus a valid justification (subset/specificity argument or correct probabilities/formulas). Give part marks if the order is right but justification is incomplete or has a minor error, or justification is right but order is stated slightly wrongly. A wrong order earns no marks for P1; an answer with no justification cannot earn P2.
